**Delima Pacific Academy Sdn. Bhd. – Quick Vetting Summary** | **Aspect** | **Key Points** | |------------|----------------| | **Company Profile** | • **Name:** Delima Pacific Academy Sdn. Bhd.
• **Status:** Active (Private limited)
• **Incorporated:** 5 Jun 1991
• **Location:** Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
• **Industry / Business:** Education – offers professional training courses in accounting and finance.
• **Share Capital:** RM 250,000 | | **Ownership & Governance** | • **Directors:** 2 (Managing Director & Executive Director).
• **Shareholders:** Both directors are the sole shareholders – Director 1 (57.42 %) and Director 2 (42.58 %).
• **No former names** or complex ownership structures. | | **Financial Health (FY 2022‑2024)** | **Revenue Growth:** RM 25.1 M → RM 26.6 M → RM 27.5 M (≈ 3 % YoY).
**Profitability:** Net profit margin improved from 5.5 % (2022) to 7.6 % (2023) then settled at 6.8 % (2024). EBITDA margins are healthy (13.7 %‑16.4 %).
**Liquidity:** Quick ratio consistently > 1.5 (1.64‑1.80) – indicates good short‑term solvency. Cash‑to‑revenue ratio is low but improving (0.03‑0.07).
**Cash Flow:** Operating cash flow positive each year (RM 3.2‑3.8 M) with free cash flow > RM 1.8 M, supporting reinvestment.
**Leverage:** Debt‑to‑equity falling (1.49 → 1.02). Interest coverage > 6× (up to 8.8×), showing comfortable ability to service debt. | | **Operational Efficiency** | • **Asset Turnover:** ~1.4‑1.5× – efficient use of assets.
• **Days Sales Outstanding:** ~87‑93 days – moderate collection period.
• **Days Payables Outstanding:** ~88‑95 days – balanced payment terms.
• **Cash Conversion Cycle:** Turned from slightly negative (‑0.5 days) to modestly positive (≈ 1 day) – overall cash‑friendly. | | **Audit & Compliance** | • Audited by **Audit Firm 4** for the last three years.
• **Unqualified opinions** each year – no red‑flag audit issues. | | **Litigation** | No recorded legal cases. | | **Red Flags / Concerns** | • Cash holdings are modest relative to revenue (≈ 5‑6 %); the business relies on operating cash flow rather than large cash buffers.
• No inventory (service‑based), so inventory‑related metrics are N/A – not a concern for a training provider. | | **Why It May Be Worth a Deeper Look** | • Stable, growing revenue in a niche professional‑training market.
• Strong profitability and cash generation despite modest capital base.
• Simple ownership (directors are also shareholders) simplifies due‑diligence.
• Low leverage and solid interest coverage reduce financial risk.
• Clean audit record and no litigation history. | | **Potential Deal‑Fit Considerations** | • Assess the quality and relevance of its training programmes to your needs.
• Verify the credentials of its trainers and any accreditation bodies.
• Review any contractual terms related to intellectual property or curriculum licensing.
• Confirm that its cash‑flow profile can support any upfront project financing you may require. | **Bottom Line:** Delima Pacific Academy appears financially sound, well‑governed, and operationally efficient for a service‑oriented education provider. It merits a closer review, especially around curriculum quality and alignment with your project requirements.
